title: Component Order Independence Between Master Series and RECURRENCE-ID Overrides

citations.verbatim_quote:
The order of elements in the "entries" property is implementation-
   specific, e.g. entries need not be in the same order as their source
   components in the iCalendar object.

A VEVENT (or VTODO) component is a recurrence override if it has the RECURRENCE-ID property set, and the iCalendar object contains a VEVENT (or VTODO) component that does not have the RECURRENCE-ID but the RRULE property set, and the UID property values of the two components are equal.  The component without the RECURRENCE-ID property is in that case referred to as the "main component".

1.  The primary key for referencing a particular iCalendar component is the "UID" property value.  To reference an instance of a recurring component, the primary key is composed of the "UID" and the "RECURRENCE-ID" properties.

component  = 1*(eventc / todoc / journalc / freebusyc /
                     timezonec / iana-comp / x-comp)

rationale: In RFC 5545 Section 3.6, the component body of a VCALENDAR object is a sequence of components with no mandated ordering between a master recurring component and its RECURRENCE-ID override components. In RFC 5546 Section 2.1.5 and draft-ietf-calext-jscalendar-icalendar Sections 2.1.1 and 2.1.2, a component's identity and role as either the main component (UID with RRULE and no RECURRENCE-ID) or a recurrence override (same UID with RECURRENCE-ID set) are defined exclusively by its (UID, RECURRENCE-ID) primary key and recurrence properties, never by its positional index in the VCALENDAR component collection. Therefore, all store operations (editing or deleting the whole series, a single instance, or THISANDFUTURE) and timeline expansions MUST be completely invariant to the relative ordering of master and override components in the calendar.
store_implication: All store edit and delete operations across all recurrence_id and recurrence_range modes MUST produce identical resulting component states (up to list order) and identical timeline expansions regardless of whether the calendar component list is ordered [master, override_1, ...] or [override_1, ..., master]. Store operations must distinguish the master component (recurrence_id is None) from override components (recurrence_id is not None) by their properties rather than relying on iteration order.
edge_cases_and_counterexamples: Order A ([override, master]) vs Order B ([master, override]): Editing the whole series (recurrence_id=None) to rename the summary must neither lose the override component in Order A nor delete the master component in Order B.

Single-instance edit or delete when [override_1, master] is in reverse order: Targeting an unoverridden instance of the master series or targeting override_1 by its RECURRENCE-ID must resolve the exact component via (UID, RECURRENCE-ID) rather than assuming the first component matching UID is the master.

Multiple overrides interspersed with the master component ([override_1, master, override_2]): Whole-series edits, single-instance edits, and THISANDFUTURE splits must treat the master and overrides identically to [master, override_1, override_2].

scenarios.name: whole_series_edit_order_independence_master_first_vs_override_first
scenarios.description: Renaming a 5-instance daily series that has a single-instance override on May 3 yields all 5 timeline occurrences whether the component collection is ordered [master, override] or [override, master].
